title: Ansible: inventory, playbooks, roles and idempotency

videos.script: Terraform made the machines. It cannot see inside them. Which packages are installed, what is in a configuration file, whether a service is running: none of that is in any cloud API. {{inside}} That is Ansible's job. It runs on Ana's laptop and reaches each machine over SSH. Nothing of Ansible is installed on the machines. They need SSH and Python, and Ubuntu has both. {{push}} You give it a list of machines, the inventory. Then a playbook, which says what each group of machines should look like. Install nginx. Write this page. Keep this service running. {{playbook}} Run it once, and it changes what is different. Run it again, and the summary says changed equals zero. That second run is the test you will use all lesson. {{recap}} Then the file grows up. Variables per group, and templates rendered for each host. A handler that reloads nginx only when its configuration moved. And a role that packages it all for reuse. {{role}} And at the end, the handover lesson 1 promised. Terraform writes the inventory, and Ansible reads it. {{handover}}
